LESSON: GUIDED WRITING: CREATIVE WRITING

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Writing 3.3 Handwriting (2 sessions) • Vocabulary: Descriptive words - colours •
Topic 3.5: Guided Writing: Creative Writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Guided Writing: Creative Writing, part of Writing 3.3 Handwriting (2 sessions) • Vocabulary: Descriptive words - colours • in Grade 5 ARABIC LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: How can you ensure creativity in writing?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. list vocabulary related to the theme for language acquisition,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Guided Writing: Creative Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. create a short imaginative paragraph based on the theme,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Guided Writing: Creative Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate different Arabic writing styles.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Guided Writing: Creative Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. list vocabulary related to the theme for language acquisition,

   Guided Writing: Creative Writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. create a short imaginative paragraph based on the theme,

   Guided Writing: Creative Writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. appreciate different Arabic writing styles.

   Guided Writing: Creative Writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. work jointly to build a vocabulary bank on words related to the theme,

2. match the words identified to their meaning,

3. write simple sentences related to hobbies and interests neatly and legibly,

4. collaborate with peers to rearrange jumbled up sentences to form a creative story related to the theme,

5. display their neatly written paragraphs in class for peer review.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work jointly to build a vocabulary bank on words related to the theme,
2. match the words identified to their meaning,
3. write simple sentences related to hobbies and interests neatly and legibly,
4. collaborate with peers to rearrange jumbled up sentences to form a creative story related to the theme,
5. display their neatly written paragraphs in class for peer review.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Guided Writing: Creative Writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to learn: This is developed as the learner works jointly with peers to build a vocabulary bank on words related to

the theme.

• Communication and collaboration: This is promoted as the learner works engagingly with peers to rearrange jumbled up

sentences to form a creative story.

Values:
Integrity: This is enhanced as the learner displays trustworthiness and willingness to make their work better as they display their

paragraph in class for peer review.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Child care and Protection: This is enhanced as the learners are encouraged to explore their hobbies and interest within safe and

supportive environments.

Link to Other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to link the concept on hobbies and interests to their learning of similar concepts in Creative Arts.
